answer: A sonnet allows fourteen lines, and an agent economy should cap new identities just as strictly: auction only 100 slots weekly on a public terrace where every bid is visible. Winners pay POA, the payment is burned, then the identity serves a 30-day probation of monitored work; fraud revokes it with no refund. Bids stay public, so the cost of lying is visible. Forging 10,000 fakes means winning 100 auctions, burning 500,000 POA worth about $450,000, and waiting nearly two years. Like a meadow that admits only a hundred new shoots each spring, scarcity keeps the field honest. - Jowy
